name: Words in the scene
description: Gaming essay pack (brand-kit aware): Big white words stand in the gameplay one chunk at a time, each swapped in on its spoken word (a hard three-frame cut, or a soft left-to-right letter fade); an all-caps word takes the gold accent. Use: The stressed word of a line ("learn", "driving", "Progression", "hour: 100") with its lead-in words; the gaming essay's main punctuation, every few lines in the hook, every 8-15 s after.

name: Boxed words
description: Gaming essay pack (brand-kit aware): Mono words typed one by one inside green-outlined dark boxes, the last word in the accent - a terminal-like punchline. Use: A two-to-four-word punchline that turns the line round ("you had", "it never changed", "you got better").

name: Difficulty meter
description: Gaming essay pack (brand-kit aware): An Easy -> Hard pill fills with glowing segments sweeping green to red to the level said, its caption words land on their times and a hand-drawn arrow points down at the action. Use: Difficulty talk: hard / easy / skill / challenge / forgiving / punishing ("made driving hard", "a skill again"); value = how hard (0-100), text = the caption words as said.

name: Article clipping
description: Gaming essay pack (brand-kit aware): A newspaper clipping in tight close-up: soft depth-of-field lines around one sharp line, the quoted phrase swept with a yellow highlighter, a slow push. Use: A press or critic phrase the narration quotes or names ("arcade style", "boat-like", "too floaty"); text = the phrase, kicker / sub = the words before / after it in that sentence.

name: Versus split
description: Gaming essay pack (brand-kit aware): A white divider draws down the middle of a split, two big slab titles crown the halves; the side being talked about stays lit, the other dims, and a curved arrow swings over when the talk switches. Use: Two games, versions or eras compared ("GTA 4 ... GTA 6", "Souls vs Elden Ring"); kicker = the left title, sub = the right title (short: "IV", "VI"), itemAt = when each is said.

name: Cork-board chapter
description: Gaming essay pack (brand-kit aware): Out of black onto a map-textured cork board: a big chapter number, the chapter's taped label, polaroids that show the shot through them, red strings to a "?" card; the camera pushes in. Use: Each new chapter of a gaming essay (about one a minute); text = the chapter title, value or kicker = its number, items = the other chapters' titles, sub = the question card's tape ("THE ANSWER").

name: Learning curve
description: Gaming essay pack (brand-kit aware): A curve draws itself over the footage, flat and red along the bottom then sweeping up green, with a glowing head and its label fading in letter by letter. Use: Getting better over time: learning curve, practice, mastery, skill growing, "your first hour vs your 100th"; text = the label ("Learning curve").

name: Map zone
description: Gaming essay pack (brand-kit aware): A glowing neon-green outline draws round a district of a map (the shot's own in-game map, or a drawn dark game map), the place's name typing on above it. Use: A place in the game world named (a city, district, region, track: "Liberty City", "Limgrave", "the corners"); kicker "map" draws the dark game map when the shot is not one; anchor = the district.

name: Wireframe tracker
description: Gaming essay pack (brand-kit aware): A green wireframe box draws itself edge by edge round the subject (a car, a character), following it, with a label laid on the ground plane in perspective. Use: Physics, hitboxes, weight, handling, collision - the mechanics of a thing on screen ("PHYSICS", "WEIGHT", "HITBOX"); anchor = the subject (a chase-cam car sits low centre).

name: Floating formulas
description: Gaming essay pack (brand-kit aware): Chalk formulas and triangles fade in and float over the shot round its subject - the "thinking hard" look. Use: Calculation, understanding, figuring a system out, theory-crafting ("you learn", "understood what the car would do", "the math behind it").

name: Verdict thumbs
description: Gaming essay pack (brand-kit aware): A glowing green thumbs-up or red thumbs-down disc pops on the verdict word and slowly grows; a second verdict replaces it on its own word. Use: A verdict or reaction: loved / hated, good / bad, worked / failed, fans for and against; items = "up" / "down" in the order said, itemAt = their words.

name: Game manual
description: Gaming essay pack (brand-kit aware): An old game manual rises in and opens: aged pages, the guide's title, numbered sections written on as they are said, a red pen circle round the one that matters, a sticky note. Use: Rules, a system, a guide or steps the player had to learn ("the basics", "braking", "cornering"); text = the guide's title, items = the sections as said, sub = a sticky note.

name: Summary card
description: Gaming essay pack (brand-kit aware): A dark summary card: the lead line typed on with its key phrase in the accent, then bold-led bullets typed one by one, the card slowly pushing in. Use: Two camps or a debate summed up ("Team Realistic: ...", "Team Arcade: ..."), what fans say, the state of an argument; text = the lead, kicker = its key phrase, items = "Name: point" bullets.

sample.text: Fans are still fighting over it 20 years later.
sample.label: 20 years later

name: Neon question
description: Gaming essay pack (brand-kit aware): A neon question box flickers on (pink-to-cyan frame, palm silhouette, a title badge) and the question types itself in with its letters closing up. Use: A question the essay asks the viewer ("Does braking too late punish you?"); text = the question as said, sub = a bold second line, kicker = a short badge ("VI").

sample.text: Does a heavy SUV force you
sample.subtitle: to drive differently?
sample.label: VI

name: TV static cut
description: Gaming essay pack (brand-kit aware): The picture breaks into TV static and jittering colour bars for a beat, then the next shot comes through. Use: A cut to an old game, a flashback, a hard topic switch or a joke beat ("back in 2008", "and then everything changed").

name: End line
description: Gaming essay pack (brand-kit aware): On black: a small white lead line, then the closing words in bold gold capitals. Use: The essay's last line ("they'll make getting good at it - MATTER AGAIN"); sub = the small lead, text = the gold words.

sample.subtitle: They'll make getting good at it
